channel.description: Recent content in Rock, Metal & Punk Articles and Features | Loud Legends on Loud Legends

item.title: What ANGUS YOUNG Thinks About Fans Who Rejected AXL ROSE As AC/DC’s Singer
item.description: In an interview with Rolling Stone in 2021, guitarist Angus Young opened up about a moment that split fans of AC/DC, when Axl Rose stepped in as lead singer during their 2016 tour.

item.title: The Vulnerable METALLICA Song That Set The Band On A New Path, According To JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: For a band known for thrash, fire, and a habit of rattling stadium foundations, Metallica’s transformation didn’t happen with a single riff or overnight revelation. It was a slow burn.

item.title: The Two METALLICA Songs JAMES HETFIELD Finds 'Truly Difficult' To Perform Live: 'Really Messes With Me'
item.description: Metallica has been around for over 40 years, and their music is known for being fast, loud, and often complex. But for frontman James Hetfield, two songs from their 2008 album Death Magnetic still stand out as especially difficult to play live.

item.title: How METALLICA Fooled Audiences in the Early Days, According to JAMES HETFIELD: 'We Took All The Credit'
item.description: Metallica, one of the most recognized names in heavy metal, wasn’t always the arena-dominating force it is today. Back in 1981, when James Hetfield and Lars Ulrich first formed the band, they didn’t have a vault of original songs ready to go.

item.title: Why IRON MAIDEN Turned To Japan Before Chasing The American Dream, According to ROD SMALLWOOD
item.description: Iron Maiden’s first real step onto the global stage came in 1981, the same year the band dropped Killers and hit the road for their first world tour.

item.title: The Band EDDIE VAN HALEN Believed Saved Rock ‘n’ Roll From Extinction: 'Rock Wouldn’t Exist Without Them'
item.description: Rock music has had plenty of supposed saviors. Every few decades, someone new gets the credit for dragging the genre back from the brink. Eddie Van Halen was one of those names, but according to him, his own rise might not have happened without a much earlier band shaking things up.

item.title: The One Drummer PHIL COLLINS Admired But Called Out For Having A Massive Ego: 'The Size of a Hotel'
item.description: Phil Collins wasn’t just the voice that brought pop stardom to Genesis. He also helped redefine how drums were recorded in the 1980s, built a massive solo career, and even teamed up with unexpected names, like when he played with Led Zeppelin.

item.title: The BLACK SABBATH Song That Blew Led Zeppelin's JOHN BONHAM’s Mind
item.description: Before joining Led Zeppelin and becoming a rock legend, John Bonham was already turning heads in the music scene of England’s Black Country. As a teenager, just 16 years old, he crossed paths with a fellow drummer: Bill Ward, who would later power Black Sabbath’s thunderous rhythm section.

item.title: The RUSH Album That Led to Fan Backlash, Internal Tension, and a Moment of Regret: 'It Wasn’t the Smartest Move'
item.description: Most bands with long careers eventually take a creative detour. Whether to keep things fresh or avoid burnout, they try something new. Sometimes it works. Sometimes it doesn’t.

item.title: When MAX CAVALERA Almost Reunited With SEPULTURA: 'We'll Cross Paths Again'
item.description: Max Cavalera is best known for helping create one of Brazil’s most influential metal bands: Sepultura. But in 1996, after years of success, he walked away from it all.

item.title: The Problem With 'LOAD' and 'RELOAD', According to JAMES HETFIELD: 'I Hate That Part Of Us'
item.description: Metallica made a name for itself in the early days with fast, aggressive thrash metal. But things changed with the release of their self-titled album in 1991, known to most as the Black Album.

item.title: LIMP BIZKIT's Top 5 Songs Ranked By Fans, From Deep Cuts To Major Hits
item.description: Limp Bizkit helped define the sound and attitude of late ’90s nu-metal. Known for mixing heavy guitars, rap vocals, and over-the-top energy, the band became one of the most talked-about acts of their time.

item.title: What Growing Up Was Like for DAVE MUSTAINE: 'My Dad Drank A Lot And Was Abusive'
item.description: Dave Mustaine, the founder of Megadeth and one of heavy metal’s most recognizable voices, has lived a life filled with music, fame, and success. But behind the guitars and sold-out shows is a past that’s far less glamorous.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD Reveals How the 'Terrible' LARS ULRICH Convinced Him to Start METALLICA
item.description: James Hetfield remembers the first time he met Lars Ulrich. According to him, Lars wasn’t exactly a great drummer when they crossed paths. Still, something about his energy made a lasting impression.

item.title: The AC/DC album that FLOPPED HARDER Than Expected And Nearly Turned Into A FULL-BLOWN CRISIS
item.description: Back in Black is the album everyone knows. It’s the one that sold like crazy and turned AC/DC into a global powerhouse. But not every album had the same luck.

item.title: The Backstage Incident That Made KERRY KING Call a Rock Icon a 'Complete Jerk'
item.description: Not everyone in the world of music gets along, and that includes some of its biggest stars. Even in heavy metal, a genre known for its intensity and larger-than-life personalities, there are musicians who just don’t click.

item.title: The Genre DAVE GROHL Called 'Too Easy' And Blamed for Making ROCK DUMBER
item.description: Dave Grohl has always been a believer in loud guitars, big feelings, and not overthinking things. Foo Fighters, the band he’s fronted since the mid-’90s, built a career on that formula: simple riffs, catchy choruses, and performances that sometimes go off the rails, in a good way.

item.title: THE BAND That Toured With Guns N’ Roses and Wished They Hadn’t: 'I Don’t Want To Be Around Them'
item.description: In the early ’90s, opening for Guns N’ Roses was considered a golden ticket, massive crowds, media buzz, and a shot at mainstream fame. For Soundgarden, a loud and rising band from Seattle, the offer felt like a fast pass out of the grunge underground.

item.title: The Night SLASH Felt Deep Shame Over GUNS N’ ROSES’ Treatment of METALLICA: 'I Lost Their Respect'
item.description: Back in the early ’90s, Guns N’ Roses were living the full-throttle rockstar fantasy, loud, chaotic, and unapologetic. Their shows were wild, their image untamed, and their reputation built on pushing limits.

item.title: The Emotional METALLICA Song That Wasn’t Meant to Be, According to JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: When Load dropped in June 1996, it marked a sharp left turn for Metallica. The band traded speed and aggression for a slower, more reflective sound. That shift didn’t land well with everyone, but it did show fans a broader side of the band’s musical identity.

item.title: The Unusual Way AC/DC's ANGUS YOUNG Came Up With the Chorus of 'HIGHWAY TO HELL'
item.description: Angus Young, lead guitarist and founding member of AC/DC, shared a rather unexpected story about how he wrote one of rock’s most iconic choruses. Speaking in a 2021 interview with Essentials Radio on Apple Music (via Kerrang), Young explained how the chorus of “Highway to Hell” came to him, not in a studio or during rehearsal, but while he was on a bathroom break.

item.title: The One Thing That Could End MEGADETH, According to DAVE MUSTAINE
item.description: Megadeth has been going strong for four decades, led from day one by guitarist, vocalist, and founding member Dave Mustaine. He’s the only constant in the thrash metal band’s long history and the driving force behind many of its best-known songs, including “Peace Sells,” “In My Darkest Hour,” “Holy Wars… The Punishment Due,” “Symphony of Destruction,” “A Tout Le Monde,” and “Trust.

item.title: 'The BIGGEST CLICKBAIT of All Time' Involving Megadeth’s DAVE MUSTAINE
item.description: Dave Mustaine Sentenced to Life? No, Dave Mustaine isn’t in prison. Yes, people actually believed he was. And of course, someone on YouTube made money off it.

item.title: The 'COMMERCIAL' Song AC/DC Didn’t Want To Record, And It Ended Up On The Charts
item.description: In June 1978, AC/DC got their first taste of chart action in the UK with “Rock ’n’ Roll Damnation”, which reached number 24. Nothing to throw a parade over, but for a band that had never cracked the charts there before, it was a decent showing.

item.title: The AC/DC Song They’d Rather Pretend NEVER HAPPENED: 'Really Soft Stuff'
item.description: “But the answer was literally on the other side.” Back when AC/DC hadn’t yet locked in the sound that would make them gods to some and repetitive to others, they were still fumbling through the dark.

item.title: 5 METALLICA Songs That Have Nothing to Do With HEAVY METAL, Yet WORKED BRILLIANTLY
item.description: Say heavy metal and Metallica instantly comes to mind. Since the early ’80s, the band carved out the sound, fury, and attitude of a genre that lives off shrieking guitars and bone-rattling drums.

item.title: The One AC/DC Song ANGUS YOUNG Struggles to Play Live
item.description: Few bands are as famously built on no-nonsense riffs as AC/DC. For Angus Young and his brother Malcolm, there was no mystery to their formula: loud guitars, open chords, and choruses made for the crowd to scream in unison.

item.title: Why Limp Bizkit’s FRED DURST Always Wore That RED BASEBALL CAP
item.description: Back in the early 2000s, nu metal was dominating the rock scene, with bands like Slipknot, Korn, Kid Rock, and Linkin Park in constant rotation on MTV.

item.title: The Heavy METALLICA Song That Tells the Story of JAMES HETFIELD’s Childhood TRAUMA
item.description: James Hetfield, guitarist and frontman of Metallica, didn’t exactly grow up riding rainbows. His early years were marked by the rigid dogma of a household that followed Christian Science, a belief system founded by Lafayette Ronald Hubbard (yep, the same guy behind Scientology).

item.title: The BEST SONG to Introduce Someone to KORN, According to JONATHAN DAVIS
item.description: So you want to introduce someone to Korn. Good luck. You’ve got nearly three decades’ worth of dreadlocks, detuned guitars, and unresolved childhood trauma to work with.

item.title: The GRUNGE Band JAMES HETFIELD Says 'Saved Music': 'It was exactly what music needed'
item.description: Back when rock was drowning in mousse and tight pants, Nirvana kicked down the door like a grunge-splattered SWAT team. Metallica? They’d already been tearing limbs off with thrash riffs from the Bay Area for a decade.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD’s Favorite Thrash Bands (That Aren’t METALLICA, SLAYER, MEGADETH or ANTHRAX)
item.description: At this point, saying Metallica “isn’t thrash anymore” is like complaining MTV doesn’t play music videos. Welcome to the last three decades. Sure, the band traded speed for stadiums a while back, but try telling the IRS they’re not the face of thrash metal and see how that goes.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On the 'Weak' METALLICA Member: 'Not Amazing'
item.description: James Hetfield has always been particular when it comes to Metallica’s music. Known for his precision as a rhythm guitarist, he’s often regarded as the most technically sharp member of the band, along with current bassist Robert Trujillo.

item.title: When METALLICA Brought Back 'FRANTIC' Live And JAMES HETFIELD Roasted St. Anger
item.description: Back in 2021, Metallica briefly resurrected “Frantic”, the chaotic opener from their 2003 punching bag of an album, St. Anger. The band pulled the song out of retirement for a set at the Aftershock Festival on October 8 (watch the video below), years after it had mostly vanished from live shows following a few scattered appearances in 2019 and a much longer break since 2011.

item.title: The Day KORN Knocked a Guy Out Mid-Show… and Then WROTE A SONG About It
item.description: Not every song is born in a studio with clean instruments and sober minds. Some, like Korn’s Clown, crawl out of drug-fueled all-nighters in dingy apartments, shaped as much by the chaos around them as by the riffs themselves.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On His Father's Abandonment: 'He Didn't Even Say Goodbye'
item.description: Before the arenas, awards, and global tours, James Hetfield was just a kid growing up in the suburbs of Los Angeles. The setting looked ideal from the outside.

item.title: How LEMMY KILMISTER Helped Invent THRASH METAL With ACE OF SPADES
item.description: By the late 1970s, rock had ballooned into a spectacle of arena shows, towering stage sets, and endless guitar acrobatics. Meanwhile tucked away in sweaty basements and smoky pubs, a small group of musicians were chasing something far less polished.
